newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Murdoch sees no effects from media probe.
newsitem.headline: Murdoch sees no effects from media probe.

text.p: News Corp Ltd Chief Executive and Chairman Rupert Murdoch said on Thursday he did not expect any developments for his media empire from the Australian government's review of cross-media ownership rules.

"I don't expect anything from the cross-media inquiry. Governments always have too many inquiries. We'll see how it all turns out," Murdoch told reporters after a luncheon meeting with Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge.
Murdoch later said he expected Australian-based media mogul Kerry Packer to benefit from the investigation.
Packer controls Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, which owns the top-rating Nine Network and about 15 percent of John Fairfax Holdings Ltd.

Packer has also said he wants to merge with Fairfax, but is currently prevented by rules stopping a media owner from having both a major newspaper and television station in the same city. "It'll probably turn out the way Mr Packer wants it," Murdoch told the reporters.
Murdoch's News owns about five percent of Fairfax and has Murdoch has said he would like to increase this stake.
News owns newspapers competing with Fairfax dailies in Sydney and Melbourne.
